question.text: An escrow arrangement in a PE deal is typically used to:

answer.text: Hold a portion of the purchase consideration to secure indemnification claims post-closing
Pay management fees to the fund manager

explanation.text: The Logic: In PE/M&A practice, a purchase-price escrow holds back a portion of the consideration with a neutral third party for a specified post-closing period, so that any indemnification claims arising from breach of representations and warranties have a readily available pool to draw from. If no claims arise within the agreed window, the escrow amount is released to the seller. The Trap: Escrow protects the buyer (the AIF) by ensuring funds are available to back up indemnification commitments, but it reduces the seller's immediate cash proceeds. Note: The XIX-A workbook discusses representations and warranties in term-sheet and definitive-agreement contexts and references cash/securities escrow in debt-security and debt-fund DD contexts, but does not specifically describe a PE purchase-consideration escrow as a defined mechanism. Treat purchase-consideration escrow as general PE/M&A documentation practice.
